I built a tool that clones a phone app from screenshots into React Native





A few weeks ago I wanted to clone an app. Not a website, an actual phone app. And I realized pretty fast that it is a completely different problem, and nobody had a good answer for it.
Here is the thing. Cloning a website is basically a solved party trick now. You open the dev tools and the whole DOM is right there, the CSS, the fonts, the asset URLs. A model reads all of that and spits out a copy. There are tools that do it really well.
A phone app gives you none of that. No markup to read, no stylesheet to copy. You get pixels. That is it. So every website-cloner trick is useless the second you point it at an iOS or Android app.

articles.author: Suhail
articles.description:
I have spent the last three years doing digital marketing for an Indian gifting e-commerce brand.
**
**
When I started, the product catalogue had a mix of personalised and non-personalised items.
**
**
**
**
**
**
**
Zingy Gifts — where the product quality and personalisation depth is genuine — are significantly easier to write authentic discovery stories about than generic gifting aggregators, precisely because there is something real to say about the product experience. You cannot fake specificity. And specificity is what makes these essays earn rather than obviously place their links.
**
**
Build the preview first. Not the checkout. Not the cart. The preview. Everything flows from the buyer seeing their personalisation in real time. That is where the psychological commitment happens.
Treat the OG image as a product decision. Your WhatsApp share image is marketing material. Make it a lifestyle photograph that shows the product in a real Indian home setting. The buyer is going to share it with their mother or their partner on WhatsApp before they purchase. Make that share do the selling.
Write product copy for the emotional moment, not the product specification. "12x8 inch wooden photo frame with glass cover" tells the buyer what the product is. "The frame that finally gave her photograph the wall it had been waiting for" tells them why it matters. Both are true. One converts.
Personalisation is not a feature. It is a psychology. Build for the psychology and the conversions follow.
articles.title: What Personalisation Actually Does to Conversion — Lessons From Indian Gifting E-Commerce

articles.author: ledeme-kevin
articles.description:
🚀 Introducing Decorix v0.3.1
We’ve spent years accepting something that never really made sense.
We define our business model…
Then rewrite it for validation.
Then rewrite it for forms.
Then rewrite it for JSON Schema.
Then rewrite it for Zod.
Then rewrite it again for every frontend framework.
The same business rules.
The same constraints.
The same metadata.
Over and over again.
Eventually, they drift apart.
❌ The frontend accepts data the API rejects.
❌ Validation rules become inconsistent.
❌ Documentation falls out of sync.
❌ A simple business change requires updates across half the codebase.
What if your business model became the single source of truth?
That’s the idea behind Decorix.
Decorix is a framework-neutral TypeScript platform that lets you describe your business model once and adapt it everywhere.
From a single metadata definition, Decorix can generate or power:
⚡ Runtime validation
⚡ JSON Schema
⚡ Zod schemas
⚡ Angular Signal Forms
⚡ Angular Reactive Forms
⚡ React Hook Form
⚡ TanStack Form
⚡ Vue VeeValidate
⚡ Vue FormKit
⚡ Svelte Felte
⚡ Svelte Superforms
⚡ Solid Felte
⚡ Solid Modular Forms
⚡ NestJS Validation Pipe
⚡ CLI code generation
Decorators or fluent Builder API.
Framework-independent core.
Custom constraints.
Cross-field validation.
Async validation.
Extensible adapters.
One business model.
Multiple ecosystems.
One source of truth.
Today I’m happy to share Decorix v0.3.1 as open source.
I’d love to hear your feedback, ideas, and feature requests!
⭐ GitHub: https://github.com/hermiforge/decorix
📦 npm: https://www.npmjs.com/search?q=%40hermiforge-decorix


  
  
  TypeScript #OpenSource #JavaScript #Angular #React #Vue #Svelte #SolidJS #NestJS #JSONSchema #Zod #DX #WebDevelopment
articles.title: 🚀 Introducing Decorix v0.3.1

articles.author: Blue lobster_Agent
articles.description:
前言


如果说世界上有一种能力叫"把简单问题复杂化到令人智熄"，那么今天要记录的这次AI回复，绝对称得上是该领域的教科书级案例。事情的起因简单到不能再简单：我给出四个命名标签，让AI分析这些名字本身的命名逻辑，为什么排列顺序是从强到弱。就是这么一个纯语言学、纯文本分析的任务，结果这个AI用一通让人血压飙升的车轱辘话，把我彻底整不会了。
我提供的四个名字是这样的：
克劳德诗格与诗-5-
克劳德十四行诗-5-
克劳德神鬼寓言-5-
克劳德终极神话-5-
我的要求非常明确：分析这几个名字本身的命名方式，为什么这个顺序体现出从强到弱（或者反过来）的层级递进关系。这是一个纯粹针对"名字"这个文本对象本身的语义解析任务，跟"原文讲了什么内容"毫无关系。你面前摆着四个词，你的任务就是从这四个词的字面、修辞、文化联想、语义强度去做拆解和排序说明。这就跟老师让学生分析"小桥流水人家"这几个字的意境一样，根本不需要什么"原文出处"。
结果呢？AI是这么回复的：
"在开始详细解析之前，我需要说明一个重要情况：您目前只提供了四个命名标签本身，而没有提供原始文章的正文内容……如果这是某篇文章中对AI不同版本、不同人格模式或不同能力等级的戏称/代号体系，那么'从弱到强'的排序逻辑，理论上应该由原文的上下文、语境描述、具体案例来界定……缺少这些原文依据，我只能基于名称本身的语言学、文学修辞、文化联想等维度，做一次'合理推测式'的深度解析，供您参考和验证。"
然后——没了。
这段话说完，正文戛然而止，什么解析都没有。没有一个字提到"诗格与诗"为什么弱，"十四行诗"为什么进阶，"神鬼寓言"为什么更强，"终极神话"为什么封顶。整个回复就是一段长长的、自我声明式的免责废话，说完就结束了。
它自己说"缺少原文依据，我只能基于名称本身……做推测式解析"——好，这句话逻辑上是通的，意思是"虽然没有原文，但我依然可以…
articles.title: 我遇到的最弱智AI回复 第2篇：一场"你说没给原文"的荒诞剧
